facts.title: The Blob ran out of the Colonial
facts.text: The 1958 film's most famous scene — a packed house fleeing into the street — was shot inside the Colonial Theatre on Bridge Street. The town has re-enacted it every July since 2000.

facts.title: The town is named for iron
facts.text: Phoenix Iron Works made the Phoenix Column, a wrought-iron structural column patented in 1862 and used in bridges and buildings across the country. The foundry is why there is a town here at all.

facts.title: The Colonial has been open since 1903
facts.text: It nearly went dark in the 1990s before a nonprofit bought and restored it. It now runs first-run films, repertory screenings and live events, and anchors the Bridge Street block.

facts.title: Two waterways meet here
facts.text: French Creek empties into the Schuylkill River at the edge of town. The Schuylkill River Trail runs through, connecting Phoenixville to Valley Forge and, eventually, Philadelphia.

facts.title: Bridge Street was a bypass, then a destination
facts.text: Decades of decline after the foundry closed in 1987 left storefronts empty. The current restaurant-and-brewery strip is a rebuild, not a survival — most of it postdates 2005.
